title: Buffer Overflow in `dtoverlay_extract_override` via unbounded `strcpy`
rationale: The function receives value_size but line 2101 uses strcpy without consulting it. The literal is only checked for NUL termination, not destination capacity.
attack_surface: A crafted device-tree override literal can exceed the caller's fixed 256-byte destination.
remediation: Replace `strcpy(override_value, literal_value)` with a bounded copy such as `snprintf(override_value, value_size, "%s", literal_value)` or perform explicit bounds checking against `value_size` before copying.

title: Resource Leak / Memory Leak on Error Path in OpenVideoCoreMemoryFileWithOffsetAndSize
rationale: The error path closes memFd and frees newHandle, but does not free newHandle->symbol or labels already allocated with vcos_strdup. The model's evidence was incomplete, but the leak exists.
attack_surface: Malformed or unreadable VideoCore symbol data can select an error path after allocations.
remediation: Before freeing `newHandle` at `err_exit`, check if `newHandle->symbol` is non-NULL, iterate through allocated `sym->label` strings up to the processed count, free them, and free `newHandle->symbol`.

title: Integer Overflow in Memory Bounds Check and Size Calculation leading to Out-of-Bounds Memory Access
rationale: Both the end-address check and mmap size calculation add attacker-influenced numeric values without overflow-safe subtraction checks.
attack_surface: A large address/length pair supplied to the memory-access API can wrap unsigned arithmetic.
remediation: Validate `numBytes` and perform overflow-safe arithmetic checks (e.g. ensure `numBytes <= vcHandle->vcMemEnd - vcMemAddr + 1` and check for overflows before calculating `mapSize`).

title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow in string override parsing
rationale: The decode loop and final terminator increment q without checking it against the 256-byte unescaped_value array.
attack_surface: An override string longer than 255 decoded bytes writes beyond a stack buffer.
remediation: Check the buffer boundary before appending characters to `unescaped_value`. Ensure `(q - unescaped_value) < (sizeof(unescaped_value) - 1)` inside the processing loop, or dynamically allocate a buffer large enough to accommodate the unescaped output.

title: Stack Buffer Overflow via `strcpy` on `target_value`
rationale: Line 1859 performs an unbounded strcpy into target_value. No local length check precedes the copy.
attack_surface: An oversized override value reaches a static 256-byte destination.
remediation: Use `snprintf` or `strncpy` with proper bound checks and ensure null-termination, e.g., `snprintf(target_value, sizeof(target_value), "%s", override_value);`.

title: Stack Buffer Overflow via `memcpy` on `prop_name`
rationale: name_len controls memcpy and the subsequent terminator into prop_name[256] without a capacity check.
attack_surface: A crafted override property name can produce name_len greater than 255.
remediation: Check `name_len` against `sizeof(prop_name) - 1` before performing `memcpy`, and return an error if `name_len` exceeds the buffer capacity.

title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow via Unbounded sprintf
rationale: sprintf is unbounded and strlen is used only to select a slash. Exploitability depends on whether every external caller constrains overlay_dir.
attack_surface: A caller-controlled overlay directory longer than DTOVERLAY_MAX_PATH minus the suffix can overflow map_file.
remediation: Replace `sprintf` with `snprintf(map_file, sizeof(map_file), ...)` and check the returned length to ensure truncation did not occur before opening the file.

title: Integer Overflow Leading to Heap Buffer Overflow in dynstring_set_size Sizing Suffix Calculation
rationale: size * 5 can overflow before realloc. Practical reachability depends on upstream DTB and process-size constraints.
attack_surface: A very large requested dynamic-string size can overflow signed int growth arithmetic.
remediation: Check for integer overflow prior to multiplying `size * 5` in `dynstring_set_size`, or use standard safe arithmetic functions / size checking before allocation.

title: Unchecked malloc return value leads to NULL pointer dereference
rationale: malloc(prop_len) is immediately passed to memcpy without a NULL check. This is a reliable availability flaw under allocation failure.
attack_surface: Memory exhaustion after fdt_setprop_inplace fails causes a process crash.
remediation: Check whether prop_data is NULL after calling malloc. If malloc fails, return an appropriate error code (e.g., -FDT_ERR_NOSPACE) before attempting to copy or call fdt_setprop.
